articles.title: 2023 - Nikolas Ntourtourekas: The 'Spy Spell' and the 'Dark' Ritual That Led to the Death of the 19-Year-Old
articles.author: Σύνταξη in.gr
articles.excerpt: New revelations about the circumstances of death of the 19-year-old student in Spata, linked to black magic rituals.

image.alt: Nikolas Ntourtourekas and ritual objects

content.value: The family of 19-year-old student Nikolas Ntourtourekas, who was found dead in his room in Spata on July 14, 2022, is seeking answers about the objects he left behind, disputing the possibility of suicide.
According to the program 'Light in the Tunnel', his mother found him hanged in his bedroom wardrobe, with his hands tied behind his back.

The findings indicate involvement in black magic and occult rituals. A handwritten note was found titled 'Spy Spell', which appears to have been written the night of July 13th, during the year's largest full moon.
In the dining room there were two red chairs and dark symbols, suggesting the possible presence of another person during the ritual.

The note contained instructions for a ritual aimed at 'spying' on someone's feelings, with reference to specific ingredients. The last comment read: 'Leave it aside, ready for the next morning'. The next morning, Nikolas was found dead.
His father mentioned that Nikolas had shown interest in Satanism, while his brother noticed distant behavior and involvement in dark practices, such as using black candles and drawing pentagrams.

content.value: The 40-year-old perpetrator, with a history of psychiatric hospitalizations, attacked natural gas workers with gunfire claiming he had been 'bound with black magic'. The incident on Tatoiou Street resulted in 1 dead and 1 injured, while the perpetrator was arrested while preparing for further attacks.

Key elements of magical delusion: a samurai outfit as ritual attire, obsession with demonic influences ('Satan made me do it'), and paranoid accusation of victims for 'magical actions' through their work.

content.value: Voodoo, black magic rituals, spells and magic powders — these are what the Deputy Prosecutor of the Supreme Court, Mr. G. Sanidas, has been learning about lately, studying testimonies about the activities and contacts of the para-judicial network. The endless case file compiled on instances of corruption in the Justice system reveals serious allegations.

Kechagiас, presenting himself as a businessman, exploited his 'connections' to receive favorable treatment from the Justice system. On June 23, 2004, Kechagiас drew up a private agreement with a private author of 'black magic' books, aimed at facilitating banking transactions, mainly for obtaining loans.

This business had ties to Kechagiас, who offered to 'clean it up', but the cooperation yielded no positive results.

The businesswoman refers to rituals taking place in a large hotel in the Kato Patisia area. Kechagiас's collaborations were not limited to this business, as he expressed interest in acquiring another troubled cosmetics business in Corinth, which had been found to be producing amphetamines.
The presence of magical rituals and dark practices within the business world of the Justice system raises concerns about their impact on public confidence in judicial integrity and law enforcement.

articles.title: Renaissance of Magic in Athens - 1924
articles.author: Κ. Φαλτάιτς
articles.excerpt: The case of the Beautiful Church and the injury of stockbroker Hatzipanagiotis spark Athenians' interest in spiritualism, hypnotism and occult sciences.

image.alt: Renaissance of magic in Athens (1924)

content.value: Renaissance of Magic in Athens – 1924
The vision of the 'Beautiful Church' continues to hold Athenians in a state of excitement, which we can say is advancing day by day on an upward scale.

The stockbroker Hatzipanagiotis, who was found with five serious bullet wounds beneath a pine tree at the Beautiful Church, has not yet managed to gather his memory and tell the forensic doctors, the investigating authorities and journalists how and where he was wounded.

The gap that exists at this point in his memory and the involvement, at the margins or at the center of the whole affair, of various persons who have a connection to the practice of so-called occult sciences — whether hypnotism, magic, or divination — gave occasion both to the Investigation and to investigative journalism to consider whether behind the crime of the Beautiful Church one should seek not only the woman, but also spiritualism, hypnotism, divination, astrology and in general the entire mysterious medley of occult science.
The drama played out around the wounding of stockbroker Hatzipanagiotis coincided with the most topical period for Athenians.
Never before had Athenians been so interested in psychic phenomena and their investigation as they are today.
From Tahrán Bey, the fakir who appeared in Athens a year ago, to the pseudo-fakirs and pseudo-hypnotists who followed, Athenians have advanced greatly in psychic matters.
Today almost everyone is involved with spiritualism, hypnotism, dream interpretation, palmistry, suggestion and influence, and the branches of occult science.
Compared to Europe and America, where thousands of spiritualist organizations operate and hundreds of magazines are published, Athenians are still considered behind.
The Painter Apostolidis
In the Hatzipanagiotis drama two figures appear to hold the threads of the mystery: a coffee-cup reader who predicted the attack, and the painter I. Apostolidis, who is said to have hypnotized him.
Apostolidis, known for his character and artistic talent, does not appear to be connected to those responsible for the drama.
Every summer he travels to Skiathos to capture the landscapes that Papadiamantis rendered through writing.
His return to Athens is expected to shed light on aspects of the drama, especially those concerning the character of Hatzipanagiotis and the hypnotic experiments.
Spiritualism in Athens
Athens appears to be in a period of renaissance of magic, as are other European and American metropolises.
Several Societies for Psychical Research have recently been founded, the most well-known being those under Mr. Tanagras and the 'Dawn'.
At the same time the number of doctors applying hypnotism and suggestion as therapeutic means is increasing, as is their use by the police.
Magic is becoming a profession, often more lucrative than the rest.
It remains paradoxical that works of well-known spiritualist scientists have not yet been translated into Greek.
However, with the spiritualist frenzy of the era, the publication of an entire spiritualist library is expected.
Author: K. Falteits

articles.title: A Thousand Sorcerers in Athens and Piraeus 1933 - Barmpanastasis and His Devils
articles.author: Ε. ΘΩΜΟΠΟΥΛΟΣ
articles.excerpt: Athens was 'flooded with sorcerers'. A report on charlatans who exploit the naive, the distinction from scientific mediums, and the case of Barmpanastasis.

image.alt: A thousand sorcerers in Athens and Piraeus - Barmpanastasis and his devils (1933)

content.value: A Thousand Sorcerers in Athens and Piraeus 1933 – Barmpanastasis and His Devils
SCIENTIFIC MEDIUMS AND SORCERERS WHO FLEECE THE HANDBAGS OF NAIVE WOMEN.—BARMPANASTASIS WITH THE FAKIR'S HANDWRITTEN MANUSCRIPT.—RECIPES THAT BRING HAPPINESS.

Athens was flooded with… sorcerers! The Police and specifically the Morality Department cannot keep up with the chase of these strange characters who, amid phantasmagorical staging of red curtains and skulls, promise credulous clients — and above all their endless female clientele — the return to the arms of unfaithful lovers, marriage to wealthy bridegrooms, and in a word, paradise on earth.

The phenomenon is not entirely new to the Greeks. It begins from the era of the Oracle at Delphi, and the historiography of this profession tells us that one of its most important victims was, in the previous century, Queen Amalia! To have children and not lose her throne, the unfortunate queen spent fortunes on sorcerers and witches.
THEY EVEN HAVE CLUBS

Lately however this exotic profession has seen astonishing growth. There is hardly an Athenian or Piraean neighbourhood that does not have its own 'den', where gods and demons are summoned and ordered with incomprehensible words and strange recipes to grant the desired happiness to clients. This astonishing growth, unchecked despite severe court penalties, has two main causes.
The first and foremost is popular misery combined with immorality. Poor girls who surrendered to merciless lovers believe that with the help of sorcerers they will legitimize their relationships.
Others again believe they will achieve a lucrative profession. Countless are those who pay the sorcerers and witches handsomely, with the idea of learning the winning lottery number from their lips.

The second and perhaps more important cause is the spread of theories of the Society for Psychical Research. Its scientific work, directed with such noble passion by Mr. Tanagras, has been misunderstood by the naive. The Society has trained numerous mediums who work under police protection. But their work is purely scientific (hypnotism, telepathy and clairvoyance) and has no connection with the sorcerers pursued by criminal law.

To combat those who prey on the wallets of the naive, they have formed a club whose board consists of the ladies Nikolaidou, Zakynthinou, Karyati, Kassandras and Pavlatou, with honorary president Mrs Alexandra Choremi.
But the unofficial sorcerers have also formed a club among themselves to advance their interests and anticipate police pursuit.
Police sergeant Mr. N. Panagiotopoulоs assures us that approximately one thousand sorcerers and witches have magnificent 'dens' in Athens and skim the wallets of the naive.
As the ace of aces in this diabolical profession, the police have characterized Anastasios Vlysidis, called Uncle Anastasis by his clientele.
He has acquired from his profession a three-storey mansion on Ferron Street, and his clientele comes three-quarters from the upper social class.
Just a month ago the Police closed the gates of his most luxuriously furnished den, following an anonymous letter.
His brazenness was such that he did not hesitate to declare both to the Police and to the Court that a fakir had entrusted him with a manuscript on whose pages were written all the recipes.
With these, he added, all the spirits arrive immediately and obey his wishes.
He was asked to produce the manuscript. He answered that he had chewed it and it was in his stomach.
— Why? asked the police officer Mr. Pantelis.
— Because that was the order of my arch-sorcerer father. I swallowed it once I had memorized its contents, but I haven't digested it. It remains intact in my stomach.
— My assistants are together with the manuscript in my belly. Pay attention here and be quiet.
At his prompting the door of the police office was closed. The most likely explanation is that he wanted to hypnotize all the police officers — and he succeeded.

The enormous belly of the bulky Barmpanastasis began to swell dangerously. It reached his chest. It swayed left and right. The police officers had been so hypnotized that they told him to stop, believing he was about to burst like a balloon.
He was also bellowing like a buffalo and then said:
— See, I have them inside me and I do whatever I want with them. Watch!
He then waggled his finger and an inkwell on the table in the other corner fell down, without anyone having touched it.
The scientific explanation is that the crafty uncle possesses psychokinesis. /
Not even his psychokinesis was accepted by the court, which convicted him. Which is curious, given how many victims he had and the wealth he accumulated through their faith in him.
The room where he worked in the luxurious mansion on Ferron Street was filled with black drapes. Black also the furniture and below it a skin from an all-black bear.
Only he was in white, seated on a very low round stool. He wore a white turban, a white caftan, and embroidered on his chest a bony hand.
'Mademoiselles' and ladies who entered one by one were seized with a shudder.
The contrast of the black décor with the white exotic outfit was enough to fill naive clients with awe.
The local fakir spoke abruptly: — Quickly! What do you want?
His voice was deep and cavernous, as required by the craftiness of the business.
Drawn roughly on his right palm were a skull and two bones.

He would open his palm as the client sat before him trembling and after a few moments would tell her her full name — making the naive victim feel even greater trust in this superhuman Uncle Anastasis.

And the phenomenon, as Mr. Tanagras explains, is the simplest: it involves the power of self-concentration and telepathy, which many people possess, though they cannot change the fate or will of others, as charlatans promise.

In any case, the victims received their recipe written on little red pieces of paper, which they had to execute at the first hour of every night, the first day of the week, and the first day of the month.
They had, after memorizing the contents, to chew and swallow them without another human eye seeing them — otherwise they lost their magical power.
The purpose of this order was obvious: he took care to leave no evidence. But with this wish, he caused all his victims to later resort to pharmacists for laxatives.

articles.title: Discovery of a Skeleton in Piraeus – Is it Magic? 1925
articles.excerpt: The skeleton of an elderly person is found near the Piraeus ISAP station, with witnesses speaking of witches, sorcery and possible crime.

image.alt: Discovery of a skeleton near the Piraeus ISAP station in 1925

content.value: Mystery surrounds the skeleton found near the Piraeus ISAP station. It has not yet been established who was the elderly woman who abandoned the skeleton among the refuse.
The police sub-inspector of the 3rd Precinct, Mr. P. Barmpetseas, who is conducting the relevant investigation, has formed the opinion that the matter involves sorcery.

Maria Georgios Marketou, a neighbourhood resident, was questioned and testified that witches in Piraeus use human skeletons either by burning the bones into powder or exposing them to rain for the extraction of omens.

The elderly woman, who appears to have been one of them, left the skeleton uncovered so it would get wet. The number of such witches, according to testimonies, increased after the arrival of refugees from Asia Minor, most of whom reside in Kokkinia.
Witness Vas. Giakoumakis testified that a neighbourhood child saw the elderly woman, dressed in black, emptying the bones and lighting a fire at the spot — an act considered a sign of sorcery.
Despite the indications of magic, the possibility of a crime cannot be excluded. Perhaps the skeleton belonged to a victim that the elderly woman was keeping and abandoned out of fear of exposure.
The skeleton was almost complete, with the bones detached and bearing clear signs of age. It was sent to the forensic laboratory of the University for examination.

content.value: Into a municipal well near Peukakia, a soap effigy of a baby wrapped in cloth and adorned with pins, cigarette remnants and matches was thrown a few days ago by unknown women.

As was to be expected, a neighbour who spotted the two women hastened to spread throughout the neighbourhood that an unknown person had thrown a newborn baby into the well. The neighbourhood was immediately thrown into uproar and the police precinct was notified. Police officer Mr. Vergogiannopoulos sent a letter to City Hall announcing the situation and requesting a specialist to clean the well. Mr. Benakis yesterday dispatched City employees who, after searching inside the shaft, hauled up the notorious effigy.

It appears that this involves some form of sorcery. The police are conducting investigations to discover the witch who threw the neighbourhood into confusion. The notorious effigy was transported to a deserted location accompanied by the cross-making neighbours.
Note: In the preceding days all of Athens had a water shortage issue and was searching for ways to bring water to the aqueducts, though the incidents may not be related.

articles.title: The Full Moon Drove the Satanists Wild - Volos 1992
articles.excerpt: A night of Satan-worship in Volos sparked by the full moon, with black magic rituals in ruins and groves. Parents and the Church in uproar, while police consider the matter unfounded.

image.alt: Archival image from the 1992 Apogevmatini newspaper article, p. 10

content.value: A night of Satan-worship for the young members of the coordinating organization active in Volos. The full moon was merely the pretext. Black magic rituals were organized at many points throughout the entire prefecture.
Inside ruined and abandoned houses, in remote groves and even in fields. The young people erected altars of worship to Satan, lit candles and sang hymns dedicated to him.

Whispers about the nocturnal activities of the Satanist organization have been spreading since early morning over the city. Most parents were alarmed, fearing their own children might inadvertently be initiated into paganism during the night. Not a few turned to both the Police and the Church, requesting special policing measures.

The police however consider the matter essentially unfounded. 'We have no proof as to whether such rituals are genuinely taking place in our city. Only indications and the reports of the Metropolitan. My personal opinion is that some children are simply having fun in an unusual way,' said a police officer from the Volos Police Directorate late in the evening.

The clergy of the area express their intense concern about what is taking place. They ask students to be careful and address the 'wayward' emphasizing that if they repent, the Church is ready to welcome them. 'They may have fallen into great errors. Repentance is necessary and they shall be found in our fold,' they characteristically say.

articles.title: Black Magic Ritual in Chalcis - 1994
articles.excerpt: Satanic symbols, nails and mysterious prayers were found at the Chalcis Lighthouse, left by a mysterious woman. The Church intervened and the finds were exorcised and burned.

image.alt: Archival image from the 1994 Evvoiki Gnomi newspaper article

content.value: The nightmare of black magic hangs over Chalcis, as there are still individuals who engage in mysterious rituals, spells and prayers to Satan.
Satanic symbols, nails and mysterious prayers were found in the Lighthouse area, left by a mysterious woman. The 'Gnomi' dealt with the case on Tuesday after an anonymous reader phone call.
The Satanic symbols were found inside a bag, exorcised by a priest and burned following actions by our newspaper and the Holy Metropolis.

The chronicle: Around 10 in the morning a reader called 'Gnomi' anonymously and reported seeing a tall, slim, dark-haired woman in a red jacket placing a plastic bag in the sea at the shore beneath the Lighthouse grove. She anchored the bag under the sea with a stone.

A little later the bag began to float. The two men who had witnessed it retrieved the bag and found Satanic symbols: a wooden tablet with Satanism symbols (pentagrams, dragons etc.), numbers from 1 to 64, and nails.
There were also papers with incomprehensible notes, a black stone and a text in an incomprehensible dialect resembling a prayer to be read 400 times. The name 'Vosilis' was written on the papers.
The two men called the police, who said they would only intervene following a named complaint, noting that the mere existence of the symbols is not a criminal offence.
The reader then called 'Gnomi', which turned to the Holy Metropolis. The Protosyngkellos sent Archimandrite Ioannis Theodorakopoulos to examine the finds.
Fr. Ioannis ruled that the items were indeed Satanic symbols, read a prayer of exorcism at the spot, and all the finds were consigned to the flames.

articles.title: Black Magic Rituals Volos - The Students of Satan - 1992
articles.excerpt: An open secret across all of Volos: black magic rituals by secondary school students, with a leader who 'kills with his gaze'. The Holy Metropolis of Dimitriados and preacher Fr. Daniel have been investigating the network for months.

image.alt: Archival image from the 1992 Eleftheros Typos newspaper article, pp. 32-33

content.value: — An open secret across the entire city: the black magic rituals and the leader who kills with his gaze.

'I came for you to read the prayer over my child, Father. He found a skull smeared with candles and plaster on the beach and came home terrified. His classmates do it, he says — works of Satan, diabolical things...'

The cry of anguish of the distressed mother fell like a thunderbolt on the Holy Metropolis of Dimitriados Volos, a little after Easter. It was the first report on the network of Satanist students that had for two years been infesting the schools of Volos, the thread for Metropolitan Christodoulos and Fr. Daniel to unravel...

Now Volos knows. Publications like yesterday's front page of 'E.T.' 'Black magic rituals by students of Volos' may have surprised all of Greece, but they were no bolt from the blue for the Thessalian city. The city's young people, for the most part, know about the students' acts of worship towards Satan — everyone has seen or heard something.

During break, in the schoolyard, at the café, the secondary school students of Volos openly discuss the 'rituals held at the full moon in the Goritsa grove', and describe the 'well-known' student-leader of the network, but give no names — only whispering, because 'those people' have 'that distant gaze that if you say something more, something bad might happen to you...'

How many of the 4,000 students of Volos's secondary schools are currently caught in Satan's net? 'Unknown,' admits preacher Danail Pourtsouкlis, appointed by Metropolitan Christodoulos to deal with matters of heresies and para-religion. 'The Metropolis's investigation has revealed that there are at least three different groups of student-propagandists of Satan-worship within the schools.
They gather children in abandoned houses in Volos or in the countryside and perform black magic rituals. Inspired by books and television, with the guidance perhaps of older people from Athens.'

The most 'popular' proselytizers: 'the triumvirate of final-year sixth-form students, with a female Satanist — a graduate herself.' Fr. Daniel knows the full name of the young man who 'goes out and tells children that Satanism will offer them success, and tries to impress his classmates and make them his subordinates through threats.' He knows that rituals with skulls and lit candles take place in Volos. No grave has been found desecrated.
Has anyone ever been endangered or injured in the rituals? The priest's refusal to answer breeds anxiety in the mind.

'I approached one of the leaders through a third party. I tried to inform his parents. They spoke of youthful nonsense and didn't care.' Then the threatening phone calls to the Holy Metropolis began. 'Altered voices telling me they would kill me, ordering me to stop the investigation...'

Technical, Polykladiko, 3rd, 5th, 1st Lyceum of Volos and secondary schools. The student world buzzes. The alphabet here gets mixed with Satan's symbols in the 'margins' of notebooks and the Solomonic mingles with school textbooks, as the children say.

'Did you come about the Satanism in the schools?' the theology teacher of the 3rd Lyceum, Papa-Ioannis Pappas, will ask. 'Quite a few children have gotten involved in Satanism. In Goritsa there is a grove where students gather when there is a full moon and perform mysterious rituals over circles and crescents drawn in the soil.' He too knows the 'leader' by name.
'I talk to them in class and there is also a relevant chapter in Religious Education.'

The students talk about Satanism in their schools as if discussing football, assuring they themselves stay away out of fear. 'If you join the network and perform a ritual, you've moved far from Christ. And if you say something about what you saw, something bad can happen to you. But curiosity pushes many people towards the rituals.'
No one speaks openly, 'better not to get labelled.'

About seven cats hung on the same branch in the park, a student will say, and another: 'There are candles, knives, words, keys of Satan and symbols carved in the desks.' A classmate describes triangular burns that 'some girls have on their wrist.'

'He's well-known to everyone,' they all say about the 'leader' of the diabolical network. 'He lives in Volos, he's in the sixth form, he has the Solomonic.' The children do not reveal the 'leader' of evil. 'It's also those eyes of his that look at you strangely, piercingly. Whatever you hear about him, believe it...'

articles.title: Church Burning by Satanists - Orchomenos 1995
articles.excerpt: On Christmas Day Satanists burned the church of Panagia Skripo in Orchomenos Boeotia, the second church destroyed in the area within 8 months. Meanwhile a couple was found dead in Sitia Crete with black magic symbols.

image.alt: Archival image from the 1995 Adesmeutos Typos newspaper article, pp. 24 & 41

content.value: Monday noon. Christmas Day. Dark moments for Christendom on the day of its greatest celebration: at the very hour when Christians bow reverently before the miracle of birth, others set fire to a church and stir public opinion.
Black magic rituals, sending a shiver even through the most composed observer, unfolded in Orchomenos Boeotia, branding its small society for the second time within 8 months.

The church of Panagia Skripo is reduced to ashes. Sculptures, frescoes, icons and the entire narthex are destroyed by the audacity and impiety of those who celebrate Satan on the day of Christ's birth.
The small community is shaken. The parish priest, Father Charalampos Hatzacharalamрous, describes the incident and his eyes fill with tears.
The Firebomb

'As soon as the Christmas Day liturgy ended, we went home to eat. I lay down for a while. Suddenly I heard a child calling out: "The church is on fire, Father." I immediately got up. The church was engulfed in flames,' Father Charalampos tells us, his voice breaking.
'This is the second time. At Easter I had given a sermon to the youth about Satanism, at the Saints Anargyroi church. The same day someone called and told me: What you did, you will regret it.'
'Two days later the Saints Anargyroi was engulfed in flames, completely destroyed. Just like the Panagia on December 25th. A windowpane is broken — that is where they set fire.'

The residents of Orchomenos are in uproar. Mrs Soulou Vassiliki says: 'They've destroyed us for the second time. This church was respected by Turks, Bulgarians and Germans but was not respected by Greeks. Here the greatest miracle happened, when the Panagia herself stopped the German tanks. And now the atheists have burned it.'
Giorgos Tatsis is categorical: 'What happened is a crime. The Fire Service told us it is impossible it was caused by candles or oil lamps. A human hand did it.'

The church was built approximately 1,120 years ago from the materials of an Early Christian temple. Two young people were married there that afternoon against the backdrop of the flames. 'I called them to say the church had burned and the wedding could not take place. They said they didn't care, that they had made a vow to get married there. The whole village came to help with the clean-up.'
The damage is not only incalculable but irreparable. Father Charalampos weeps whenever he shows the miracle-working icon of the Panagia, which survived the destruction.

At the very hour when Christ was being born, Satanists were revelling in black magic rituals. They burned a church in Orchomenos in glory of the 'god of darkness' and committed abominations upon the Holy.

Meanwhile a couple was found dead in Sitia Crete, with one of the two bodies beheaded. In their car were found symbols and objects of black magic rituals. On the man's body a pendant was found with 666 engraved — the symbol of the Antichrist.

Church bodies and former Satanist members express fear that we are on the verge of new crimes. They maintain Satanists now act earlier than predetermined ritual dates to avoid detection by police and neighbours.

'This is a new tactic. They do not follow the predetermined Satanist dates and act swiftly outside their temples,' reports a former top member of Satanists in Crete. 'They steal bones, desecrate cemeteries and do not hesitate to kill to subsequently carry out their dark rituals.'

Cases such as the little girl who wrote a letter to Satan and subsequently committed suicide, the abductions of girls, and the host of reports about Satanist finds in secret caves all prove the point. All these elements are known to the Crete Police.
Fotis Nakos

articles.title: A Hodjas Sorcerer in Piraeus - 1893
articles.excerpt: A hodjas in Piraeus was deceiving women with promises of love potions, extracting over 500 drachmas from an unfortunate schoolteacher, until the police intervened following a complaint of fraud.

image.alt: Archival image from the 1893 To Asty newspaper article

content.value: Until now most sorcerers were elderly women and itinerant Gypsies exploiting simple people. But now a hodjas appears in Piraeus, duly claiming the title of sorcerer.

Some time ago a retired schoolteacher named Eleni, very unhappy in matters of love, had fallen victim to a well-known witch, hoping to hold back her lover through various potions. The police intervened and the investigation proved she had given enormous amounts of money to the witch without any change in her unfaithful lover.

His refusal to stop being unfaithful apparently did not please the schoolteacher, and she tried to change his feelings when she heard that in Piraeus there was a pious and conscientious hodjas. The schoolteacher and a friend went to Piraeus to find him.

The hodjas received the two young women, consoled them, and began his magic tricks, referring them to return after a few days to collect the potion that would bring the desired romantic stability. The new visit continued without any improvement in the situation, apart from an improvement in the hodjas's finances.

Having already extracted over 500 drachmas — an exorbitant amount for the unfortunate schoolteacher — the hodjas asked them to stay in his house for a week, offering his own room, to make it easier for them all to jointly invoke the relevant spirit at night.
Fortunately the matter stopped at the sorcerer's request, leaving the rest to the police, to which the charlatanism and fraud of the hodjas sorcerer were reported.

articles.title: The Modern Witches - 1933
articles.excerpt: Satirical article on the witches of the era and their methods: from pin-studded soap and water from thirty waves to conversing with stars and the enchantment of the eyes.

image.alt: Archival image from the 1933 Ethnos newspaper article

content.value: The modern witches are not ordinary beings, nor is witchcraft an easy business. Appearance plays a crucial role. The witch, to inspire confidence, must be a little dark or at least have the colour of filth approaching the swarthy complexion of the Gypsy.

This is the image of the witch that lives in the popular imagination. But there are also modern witches with fair complexions who practice this profession as amateurs. Such a witch could be your pretty neighbour, ready to read your cards or reveal your secrets in the coffee cup.

Magic tricks are not easy work either. The most common form of sorcery among today's witches is the pin-studded soap. The man who reported to the police the young lady who had cast a spell on him presented this Satanic contraption: a piece of soap, a piece of cloth and a few pins.

It is well known what power soap contains — which witches systematically avoid when it comes to washing themselves, yet consider indispensable for magic. Besides soap, mysterious power is also contained in water collected from thirty waves. For this one obviously needs great patience, first choosing the location with great care. Glyfada, for example, is unsuitable, as is every beach that hosts mixed bathing — considered worldly and slightly depraved places.
Furthermore, the collector of waves must know how to swim a little, in case the thirtieth wave sweeps them away.

Another method is conversing with the stars, which puts to shame all astronomers who cannot manage communication with the planet Mars. Witches, without telescopes or calculations, have been conversing for so long not only with Mars but with the entire starry sky.

However the most fearsome spells are those of witches who employ only their charms and the expression of their eyes. They are those of whom the poet speaks: With a single glance of yours, witch, / From your sweet eyes / Like glass I was shattered, / And broken into eight pieces.
Whether it was eight or seven or three pieces does not matter. Suffice it that the man was shattered and the guilty party was those beautiful eyes.

The victim of such a witch is certainly also the victim of the soap and pins. He reported the young lady who cast the ineffectual silly spell on him, and said not a word about the young lady who had truly bewitched him with her beautiful eyes. That is why we assume that women have no reason to collect thirty waves when they want to drown someone. They drown him with a smile. Men are so foolish.
T. Mor

articles.title: The Witch Who Found Husbands for Servants - 1933
articles.excerpt: Maria-Katina Polymenakous was arrested for fraud, deceiving servant women with promises of love spells and finding husbands, extracting thousands of drachmas from her victims.

image.alt: Archival image from the 1933 Foni tou Laou newspaper article

content.value: Following complaints by servants Krystalia Vassiliadou and Zoe Papadopoulou, Maria-Katina Polymenakous, aged 40, was arrested yesterday at noon, charged with fraud.

The arrested woman, presenting herself as a witch, deceived the two young women and received money from them so that, through magic, she would provide them with husbands. To find her victims the witch used servant Katina Roussou as an intermediary.
Roussou, employed at the Olympos hotel on Deligianni Street, promised the victim she would take her to an exceptional witch to cure her heartaches.
The naive Vassiliadou went to 88 Agissilaou Street, to Polymenakous's lair, and recounted her romantic predicament — she loves a young man who lately tries to find pretexts to leave her.
The Spell Didn't Work

The witch undertook to soften the young man's hard heart. The young woman gave a deposit of 300 drachmas and received a small dagger which would act magically on her friend when placed under his pillow.

The night passed. The following day Krystalia found him as cold as ever. Then another visit to the witch's lair. The magic dagger was declared a temporary spell. The witch needed to study an egg, which the young woman would cut with the dagger — this would signify dominance over her beloved.

The notorious egg was studied by the witch who remained entirely naked and covered with a white sheet on the roof terrace. With her incantations she would achieve the entry of her friend's shadow inside the egg — all in the presence of witnesses, employing the celestial stars.

The unfortunate young woman gave another 2,850 drachmas. The egg was studied. She cut it with the magic dagger but her friend's heart remained unchanged. Disappointed, she turned to the General Security and reported the fraud.

During the study of the magic egg, the witch's accomplice Roussou had found another victim: Zoe Papadopoulou, a servant at a physician's home who had assembled a dowry of 35,000 drachmas but could not find a husband. Roussou introduced her to Kontopoulos, a likeable young man who quickly won her heart.

Roussou advised the new victim to go to Polymenakous for assistance. Another egg was studied under the stars and cut. The prospective bridegroom duly appeared and asked for the servant's hand. Before consent was given, information gathered revealed he was a fraudster.
The match was cancelled. It was established that the witch received 3,000 drachmas from this victim.
Police sub-inspector Mr. Sarantopoulos went in civilian clothes with a young girl to the witch's lair. The girl played the role of his fiancée.
— I want you to tell me whether my fiancée loves me, he told the witch.
— The coffee will tell. And indeed it did, for fifty drachmas.
The next day Mr. Sarantopoulos visited again — not for fortune-telling. He arrested her and took her to the police precinct, charged with sorcery and charlatanism.

In the witch's lair was a small table on which the magic eye was painted, along with various magical utensils, and a note with 150 names. The witch Maria Polymenakous was convicted to 9 days' detention for sorcery and charlatanism.

articles.title: A Thousand Sorcerers and Witches in Athens and Piraeus - 1933
articles.excerpt: Report on the methods of Athens's sorcerers, from the initial diagnosis-trap of victims to the rituals of the Pythia of Kimonos Street who caressed the moon naked on the roof tiles. Even a police officer was nearly convinced.

image.alt: Archival image from the 1933 Acropolis newspaper article

content.value: What lures the endless clientele into the clutches of sorcerers is the initial diagnosis of the victim's identity at the first visit — like the old snare that holds captive the foolish birds with just a few crumbs of bait.

Before any discussion, the sorcerer identifies to the victim his family composition, his name, the profession of his loved one and other details. The naive victim is left speechless. How does the sorcerer know so many personal things without having been told anything?

Therefore he has superhuman qualities. A police officer, Mr. Mavrotas, was nearly convinced when he arrested Dimitriadis. He first told him that he was not a commercial employee as Mr. Mavrotas had claimed.
— You are a military man, he shouted grandly. — No, no, we're in trade. — No, the sorcerer said again. Coins are falling around you. If you're not making money now you will be later.
Mr. Mavrotas tried to hide his agitation. His surprise grew when the sorcerer took him aside and told him: — My boy, you are a young man. Do you love that woman very much?
— But of course. That's why I will marry her.

Mr. Mavrotas had presented a woman of loose morals as his acquaintance. The sorcerer discerned she was not honourable and whispered: — I see that she has many men about her and you will make a mistake if you take her.
Big Tricks

All this shook the police officer. But this power, as Mr. Tanagras explains, is common intuition and telepathy that countless people possess — it only appears otherworldly to those unaware of reality. This is unknown to sorcerers' clientele and they are initially ensnared by it.
Mr. Mavrotas's duty was to arrest him and he did. — Get dressed, let's go to the police. I am a police officer.
Dimitriadis with majestic gestures shouted: — Don't move! No! You will lose your voice! Don't touch me!
The manner in which he shouted was such that Mr. Mavrotas was completely taken aback.
Then the sorcerer raised his hands high: — Lord! Lord Fanou. Burn him! And he rang the bell like one possessed for Satan to arrive.

But Satan did not appear, Mr. Mavrotas's hands were not cut off, and the sorcerer was taken to the precinct. A woman from the sorcerer's entourage attacked the police officer and bit his right hand. She too was taken to the police, where she continued to protest the arrest of a man with such great power.

Enormous trust had also been acquired by the Pythia of Kimonos Street, Provata, who not only undertook to bring back unfaithful partners but also to cure every illness. She stripped the assets of a poor woman whose child was having convulsions due to a respiratory condition that would resolve with age.

The Pythia undertook to consult the moon and her judgment — requiring hundreds of drachmas. And to consult the moon she had to undress. On nights when the moon was waning she would climb near dawn to the roof tiles and play Salome.

She would throw off her clothes and with a veil caress the moon — explaining to her clients that she was moving naked towards the peaceful Moon with the veil and caressing her aged body. She had terrorized the neighbours when they chanced to stick their heads out of their windows at dawn: she would moan or utter incomprehensible words, so that the timid frightened ones would not peek out before daybreak.
